name: Kitchen Knife
description: An eight-inch chef's knife from somebody's kitchen block. Light, quick and easy to hide; you can throw it in a pinch.

name: Shiv
description: A sharpened toothbrush or a strip of metal wrapped in tape. Ugly, small and always on you.

name: Hunting Knife
description: A fixed-blade knife with a gut hook. Good for skinning, better for the soft spot under a jaw.

name: Baseball Bat
description: Ash or aluminium, it doesn't matter. Swung with both hands it caves in a skull.

name: Crowbar
description: A steel pry bar. Opens doors, windows and car trunks (advantage on Strength checks to force them) and doubles as a club.

name: Machete
description: A long brush blade from a garden shed. Heavy enough to take a head off with a clean swing.

name: Fire Axe
description: A red-headed axe from a glass case in the hallway. Breaks down doors and anything behind them.

name: Claw Hammer
description: A plain claw hammer. Builds barricades, pulls nails and ends arguments.

name: Golf Club
description: A steel-shafted iron. Long reach for a one-handed swing, but it bends after a few good hits.

name: Sledgehammer
description: Ten pounds of steel on a wooden handle. Slow, exhausting and final.

name: Tire Iron
description: The lug wrench from a car trunk. Every car has one.

name: Police Baton
description: A collapsible steel baton. Built to subdue people; it works on the dead if you aim for the head.

name: Pitchfork
description: A long-handled hay fork. Keeps the dead at arm's length and then some.

name: 9mm Pistol
description: A semi-automatic service pistol. Each shot uses up one 9mm round and is LOUD: everything dead within blocks hears it.

name: .38 Revolver
description: A six-shot snub-nose revolver from a nightstand drawer. Each shot uses up one .38 round and is LOUD.

name: Pump Shotgun
description: A 12-gauge pump-action. Devastating up close, nearly useless far away. Each shot uses up one shell and is VERY loud.

name: Hunting Rifle
description: A bolt-action deer rifle with a scope. One shot per action (loading), but it reaches across a parking lot. Each shot uses up one .308 round and is LOUD.

name: Carbine
description: A short semi-automatic rifle, the kind police keep in the cruiser and soldiers carry. Each shot uses up one 5.56 round and is LOUD.

name: Compound Bow
description: A hunting bow with pulleys. QUIET: the dead don't come running. Each shot uses up one arrow (you can often recover them after a fight).

name: Crossbow
description: A hunting crossbow with a cocking stirrup. QUIET. One shot per action (loading); each uses up one bolt.

name: Slingshot
description: A wrist-braced hunting slingshot. Weak but silent; good for breaking a distant window to draw the dead away. Uses up one steel ball per shot.

name: 9mm Rounds
description: Loose 9mm pistol rounds. A full magazine is 15. Count every one.

name: .38 Rounds
description: .38 Special cartridges, usually found six at a time in a sock drawer.

name: 12-Gauge Shells
description: Buckshot shells for a shotgun.

name: .308 Rounds
description: Hunting rifle cartridges. The gun shop by Route 9 sold them by the box, before.

name: 5.56 Rounds
description: Rifle rounds for a carbine. Police and Guard issue; rare.

name: Arrows
description: Carbon hunting arrows with broadheads. Often recoverable after a fight.

name: Crossbow Bolts
description: Short bolts for a hunting crossbow.

name: Steel Shot
description: Steel balls for a slingshot. Marbles and hex nuts work too.

name: Leather Jacket
description: A heavy leather jacket. Teeth have a hard time getting through it.

name: Padded Winter Coat
description: A thick parka. Keeps out the cold and some of the bites.

name: Motorcycle Gear
description: A padded riding jacket and trousers with armoured elbows and knees.

name: Turnout Gear
description: A firefighter's coat and trousers: heavy, fire-resistant and bite-resistant, and very noisy to move in.

name: Kevlar Vest
description: A police-issue soft body armour vest. Stops a bullet to the chest; doesn't help your arms.

name: Riot Gear
description: A full riot suit: hard shell plates, helmet with visor, gauntlets. Almost nothing bites through it.

name: Riot Shield
description: A clear polycarbonate shield. Hold the dead off and push them back.

name: Medkit
description: A real first-aid kit: gauze, sutures, splints, saline. One medkit is enough for one serious patch-up (Field Surgery uses one up).

name: Bandage
description: A roll of gauze and tape. Used up by Field Dressing.

name: Painkillers
description: A strip of strong prescription pills. One dose per use.

name: Antibiotics
description: A course of antibiotics. Treats infected wounds and fevers. It does not treat a bite from the dead.

name: LAZARUS Antiviral
description: An unlabelled Ventara Biologics autoinjector from the lab wing, batch code LZ-7/AV. Injected before the end, it stops the LAZARUS infection at any stage.

name: Epinephrine Auto-injector
description: An adrenaline pen. One use.

name: Sedative Syringe
description: A loaded syringe of hospital or veterinary sedative. One use.

name: Rubbing Alcohol
description: A bottle of isopropyl alcohol. Cleans a wound; burns well too.

name: Canned Food
description: A can of beans, soup or peaches. One day's food.

name: Bottled Water
description: A large bottle of clean water. One day's water.

name: Preserves
description: A portion of jerky, pickled roots or berries in syrup, put up by hand. One day's food. Spoils in a day or two.

name: Flashlight
description: A sturdy LED flashlight. Bright light in a 40-foot beam. At night it also tells everything dead where you are.

name: Batteries
description: AA batteries for flashlights, radios and walkie-talkies.

name: Duct Tape
description: A roll of silver tape. Fixes nearly anything for a while.

name: Rope (50 feet)
description: Fifty feet of nylon climbing rope.

name: Lockpicks
description: A set of picks and tension wrenches. Proficient users add their proficiency bonus to open locks.

name: Walkie-talkie
description: A two-way radio with a range of about two miles. Needs batteries.

name: Road Flare
description: A red highway flare. Burns bright for 15 minutes; the dead shy from it and then follow it.

name: Lighter
description: A refillable lighter. Lights anything that will burn.

name: Matches
description: A box of strike-anywhere matches.

name: Gasoline Can
description: A red can holding about a gallon of gasoline. Fuel for a car or a generator, or a Molotov.

name: Glass Bottle
description: An empty liquor or soda bottle.

name: Rag
description: A strip of cotton cloth.

name: Steel Pipe
description: A short length of threaded steel pipe with end caps.

name: Black Powder
description: A tin of black powder from a hunting store or a box of fireworks.

name: Fuse
description: A length of slow-burning fuse.

name: Box of Nails
description: A box of framing nails, for barricades and worse.

name: Planks
description: A few boards of lumber, enough to cover a window.

name: Backpack
description: A school or hiking backpack.

name: Car Keys
description: Keys to a car parked somewhere in town, if it's still there.

name: Sleeping Bag
description: A warm sleeping bag. Late October nights are cold.

name: Binoculars
description: See what's moving three streets away before it sees you.

name: Portable Radio
description: A battery or hand-crank AM/FM radio. At 3 a.m., 101.7 FM reads names.

name: Map of Kessler Falls
description: A folded tourist map of the town and county roads.

name: Handcuffs
description: Steel police handcuffs with a key.

name: Pepper Spray
description: One good burst of pepper spray (a canister holds about three). The dead don't care; the living do.

name: Snare Wire
description: A coil of thin steel wire for snares and trip lines. One coil per snare.

name: Bag of Fertilizer
description: Garden-store fertilizer. A chemist knows what else it's good for.

name: Bleach
description: A jug of household bleach.

name: Ammonia
description: A bottle of ammonia cleaner. Never mix it with bleach, unless you mean to.

name: Thermite Mix
description: A jar of aluminium powder and rust, ready to be lit with a road flare.
